# Shiftnest Open-Shift Offers — User Stories

## Executive Summary

Shiftnest's current process of calling staff individually to fill open shifts is slow, error-prone, and places an unnecessary coordination burden on managers. This document defines eight user stories across five epics — Open Shift Publication, Shift Discovery & Claiming, Eligibility Enforcement, Manager Approval Workflow, and Notifications & Escalation — that together automate the in-app offer-and-claim lifecycle. Eligibility is enforced against each worker's maximum weekly hours (Assumption: threshold stored per worker contract record; exact value TBD) and required training tags. A 2-hour manager approval window ensures timely confirmation; unclaimed or unapproved shifts are automatically re-offered. Six identified gaps — including offer sequencing logic, re-offer escalation limits, and training data ownership — are flagged with actionable recommendations and must be resolved before sprint planning begins.

---

## Epic 1: Open Shift Publication

### Story 1.1 — Publish an Open Shift

**As a** registered manager, **I want** to create and publish an open shift with a date, time, location, and required training tags, **so that** only qualified, eligible workers are notified and coverage gaps are filled without manual phone calls.

```gherkin
Given I am logged in as a registered manager
When I submit a new shift with date, start time, end time, location, and ≥1 training tag
Then the shift is saved with status "Open"
And all eligible workers receive an in-app notification within [Target: 60 seconds — assumption to validate]

Given I attempt to submit a shift with no training tag selected
When I tap "Publish"
Then the system displays a validation error: "At least one required training tag must be added"
And the shift is not published
```

---

### Story 1.2 — Cancel an Open or Pending Shift

**As a** registered manager, **I want** to cancel an open or pending shift, **so that** workers are not pursuing a shift that is no longer needed.

```gherkin
Given a shift has status "Open" with no active claim
When I cancel the shift
Then the shift status changes to "Cancelled"
And all previously notified workers receive a cancellation alert

Given a shift has status "Pending Approval"
When I attempt to cancel it
Then the system warns me a claim is active and requires a second confirmation tap
And upon confirmation the claim is voided, the claimant is notified, and the shift is cancelled
```

---

## Epic 2: Shift Discovery & Claiming

### Story 2.1 — View Eligible Open Shifts

**As a** care worker or shift lead, **I want** to browse a filtered list of open shifts I am eligible for, **so that** I can quickly identify coverage opportunities without seeing irrelevant shifts.

```gherkin
Given I am logged in as a care worker
And ≥1 open shift matches my training profile and would not breach my weekly hours cap
When I navigate to "Available Shifts"
Then I see only those shifts, each showing date, time, location, and required training tags

Given no eligible shift exists for me
When I navigate to "Available Shifts"
Then I see the message: "No shifts available for you right now"
```

---

### Story 2.2 — Claim an Open Shift

**As a** care worker or shift lead, **I want** to claim an open shift with a single action, **so that** the first eligible person to respond secures the slot without manager intervention.

```gherkin
Given I am viewing a shift with status "Open" and I am eligible
When I tap "Claim Shift" and confirm
Then the shift status changes to "Pending Approval"
And I receive an in-app confirmation with the approval deadline displayed
And the shift is no longer claimable by other workers
And the assigned manager receives an approval request notification

Given another worker has just claimed the same shift
When I tap "Claim Shift"
Then the system displays: "This shift has just been claimed" and I am returned to the list
```

---

## Epic 3: Eligibility Enforcement

### Story 3.1 — Enforce Weekly Hours and Training Eligibility

**As a** care worker, **I want** the system to automatically block me from claiming or seeing shifts I am ineligible for, **so that** I remain compliant with my hours cap and training requirements without relying on manual checks.

```gherkin
Given claiming a shift would cause my scheduled hours this week to exceed my maximum (Assumption: cap stored per worker profile; value TBD per contract)
When eligibility is evaluated
Then that shift does not appear in my available list
And if I somehow access it directly, the "Claim" button is disabled with the message: "This shift would exceed your weekly hours limit"

Given I lack a training certificate required by the shift
When eligibility is evaluated
Then the shift is excluded from my available list entirely

Given a required training certificate on my profile has an expiry date before the shift date
When eligibility is evaluated
Then I am treated as ineligible for that shift
```

---

## Epic 4: Manager Approval Workflow

### Story 4.1 — Approve or Reject a Claimed Shift

**As a** registered manager, **I want** to approve or reject a pending claim within 2 hours, **so that** the worker has a confirmed assignment and the roster is resolved promptly.

```gherkin
Given a shift has status "Pending Approval" and < 2 hours have elapsed since the claim
When I open the claim and tap "Approve"
Then the shift status changes to "Confirmed"
And the claimant receives an in-app confirmation with shift details

Given I tap "Reject" and enter a rejection reason
Then the shift status returns to "Open"
And the rejected claimant is notified with the stated reason
And all eligible workers are re-notified of the open shift
```

---

### Story 4.2 — Automatic Re-Offer on Approval Timeout

**As a** registered manager, **I want** the system to re-offer a shift automatically when the 2-hour window expires without action, **so that** no shift is silently stranded in a pending state.

```gherkin
Given a shift has status "Pending Approval"
And exactly 2 hours have elapsed since the claim with no manager action
When the timer expires
Then the shift status returns to "Open"
And the original claimant is notified that the shift has been re-offered
And all eligible workers are re-notified
And an escalation alert is sent to the registered manager
```

---

## Epic 5: Notifications & Escalation

### Story 5.1 — Push Notification for New Open Shifts

**As a** care worker or shift lead, **I want** to receive a push notification the moment an eligible open shift is published, **so that** I can claim it before others.

```gherkin
Given I have push notifications enabled and I am eligible for a newly published shift
When the shift is published
Then I receive a push notification within [Target: 60 seconds — assumption to validate]
And the notification deep-links to the shift detail and claim screen

Given I have push notifications disabled
When the shift is published
Then an in-app badge and inbox message are created so I see the shift on next login
```

---

### Story 5.2 — Manager Approval Deadline Reminder

**As a** registered manager, **I want** a reminder [Target: 30 minutes before the 2-hour window closes — assumption to validate] when a pending claim needs action, **so that** I do not accidentally let the window expire.

```gherkin
Given a shift is in "Pending Approval" status
And 90 minutes have elapsed since the claim (30 minutes remain — assumption to validate)
When the reminder threshold is reached
Then I receive a push notification: "Action needed: shift claim expires in 30 minutes"
And the notification deep-links to the approval screen

Given I have already approved or rejected the claim before the threshold
When the reminder would fire
Then no reminder is sent
```

---

## Identified Gaps & Recommendations

| # | Gap | Recommendation |
|---|-----|----------------|
| 1 | **Offer sequencing** — "first eligible person" is ambiguous between simultaneous broadcast and sequential one-at-a-time offer | Confirm broadcast (race-to-claim) vs. sequential before Story 2.2 is built; this is the most consequential architectural decision |
| 2 | **Escalation ceiling** — no limit on re-offer cycles; a shift could loop indefinitely | Define a maximum cycle count (Assumption: 3 — to validate) after which the shift escalates to the manager as "Unfilled" |
| 3 | **Training data ownership** — unclear who creates/maintains certificates and expiry dates | Confirm whether admin uploads or workers self-certify; add an admin story to Epic 1 if the former |
| 4 | **Shift lead approval rights** — input is silent on whether shift leads can approve claims | Define a role-permissions matrix before Story 4.1 moves to development |
| 5 | **Worker withdrawal** — no behaviour defined if a claimant wants to cancel before approval | Decide if withdrawal immediately re-opens the shift; add a story if yes |
| 6 | **Notification fallback** — workers who disable push will miss shifts; SMS/email fallback not defined | Agree per-role fallback channel; update Story 5.1 acceptance criteria accordingly |

---

## INVEST Check

| Story | **I** | **N** | **V** | **E** | **S** | **T** | Verdict |
|-------|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|---------|
| 1.1 Publish Open Shift | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Pass |
| 1.2 Cancel Shift | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Pass |
| 2.1 View Eligible Shifts | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Pass |
| 2.2 Claim a Shift | ⚠️ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Rework |
| 3.1 Eligibility Enforcement | ⚠️ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ⚠️ | ✅ | Split |
| 4.1 Approve/Reject Claim | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Pass |
| 4.2 Auto Re-Offer on Timeout | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Pass |
| 5.1 Push Notification | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Pass |
| 5.2 Deadline Reminder | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Pass |

**Stories requiring action:**

- **Story 2.2 — Rework:** The concurrency scenario (two workers claiming simultaneously) introduces a race condition whose resolution depends on Gap 1 (broadcast vs. sequential). Rework after sequencing is confirmed to ensure the story is independently testable and fully estimable.
- **Story 3.1 — Split:** Bundles weekly hours enforcement, training tag enforcement, and certificate expiry into one story. **Split into** "Enforce weekly hours cap on claiming" and "Enforce training and certification eligibility." Each has a distinct data source, separate test surface, and hours enforcement can ship a sprint earlier than the certificate-expiry logic.

---

## Next Steps

1. **Resolve Gap 1 (offer sequencing)** — book a 30-minute decision session with the PM and engineering lead this week; this unblocks Story 2.2 rework and the concurrency design.
2. **Split Story 3.1** — rewrite as two stories and re-estimate before the next sprint planning; this is the highest complexity item in the backlog.
3. **Confirm training data ownership (Gap 3)** — align with HR/ops to determine whether a separate admin story is needed; without this, Story 3.1's split cannot be fully specified.
4. **Define notification fallback channel (Gap 6)** — agree push vs. SMS/email policy with the product owner and update Story 5.1 acceptance criteria.
5. **Set escalation ceiling and unfilled-shift behaviour (Gap 2)** — add the maximum re-offer count as a configurable system parameter and extend Story 4.2 accordingly.
6. **Produce a role-permissions matrix (Gap 4)** — clarify shift lead approval rights before Story 4.1 enters development to avoid a last-minute scope change.
